description: DEF CON 33 RF Village features presentations, demonstrations, and contests exploring radio frequency security, software-defined radio, and wireless protocols. Sessions cover Meshtastic LoRa reverse engineering, aerial wardriving from general aviation aircraft, cellular testbeds for IMSI catcher detection, and smartcard analysis.

talks.title: Meshtastic Under the Microscope: From Chirps to Chat
talks.teaser: Deconstructs the Meshtastic LoRa protocol layer by layer using SDRs, GNU Radio, and Python, demonstrating frame decoding and packet transmission without mobile apps.
talks.summary:
The Rise of Off-Grid LoRa Mesh Networks

Meshtastic has become a widely adopted decentralized, low-power mesh networking protocol operating over long-range LoRa radios for off-grid communication.

Demodulating LoRa Chirps with SDR and GNU Radio

Allan Riordan Ball breaks down the physical layer modulation in Inspectrum and GNU Radio, detailing how LoRa frequency chirps are formed, synchronized, and demodulated into raw bitstreams.

Dissecting Protobuf Envelopes and AES-256 Encryption

Tracing packet propagation across intermediate mesh nodes reveals how frame routing headers wrap Protobuf payloads and encrypted AES-256 application messages.

Transmitting Custom Frames with Standalone Python

Demonstrating standalone Python scripts to forge and transmit valid Meshtastic frames equips security researchers to audit and interact directly with LoRa mesh networks.

talks.title: Tactical Flipper Zero: You Have 1 Hour and No Other Equipment
talks.teaser: Walks through a time-constrained tactical scenario using an off-the-shelf Flipper Zero for rapid RF reconnaissance across sub-GHz, Wi-Fi, and Bluetooth.
talks.summary:
Time-Constrained RF Field Reconnaissance

Field operators in tactical or red-team scenarios often face unexpected equipment loss, requiring rapid adaptation using whatever portable hardware is immediately available.

Deploying the Flipper Zero Under Constraints

Grey Fox walks through an operational scenario requiring operators to locate, identify, and monitor target transmitters within a strict one-hour deadline using only a Flipper Zero.

Multi-Band Triage: Sub-GHz, Wi-Fi, and Bluetooth

Leveraging built-in sub-GHz radio analyzers, infrared capture tools, NFC sniffers, and Bluetooth discovery modules enables rapid signal detection and identification of adversary radio communications.

Tactical Tradeoffs and Portable Tooling

Evaluating the strengths and physical limitations of compact multi-tools highlights how general-purpose hacker gadgets can serve as effective tactical triage devices in emergency scenarios.

talks.title: So What The Heck Is This Radio Stuff Anyway
talks.teaser: Breaks down radio frequency fundamentals, antenna physics, filters, Shannon-Nyquist modulation theories, and Software-Defined Radio architectures for beginners.
talks.summary:
Foundations of Electromagnetic Waves

Radio communication underpins modern wireless infrastructure, yet the physical principles of RF propagation, wavelength harmonics, and electromagnetic radiation are often perceived as black magic.

Antenna Theory, Filters, and Hardware Transceivers

Exploding Lemur breaks down antenna geometries, RF filtering circuits, amplifiers, and mixer stages that convert physical radio waves into analog intermediate frequencies.

Information Theory, Modulation, and Digital Signal Processing

Exploring Nyquist-Shannon sampling theorems explains how analog waveforms are modulated (AM, FM, FSK, PSK) to transmit digital information across crowded radio bands.

Demystifying Software-Defined Radios

Software-Defined Radio (SDR) front-ends digitize raw RF spectrum, allowing flexible software demodulation and empowering hackers to explore the airwaves.

talks.title: Warflying in a Cessna: Part II
talks.teaser: Presents aerial Wi-Fi scanning research from a Cessna aircraft, analyzing antenna configurations, altitude effects, and thousands of captured airborne access points.
talks.summary:
Expanding Wireless Auditing to the Skies

While traditional wardriving maps terrestrial Wi-Fi access points from vehicles, aerial warflying from general aviation aircraft introduces unique line-of-sight propagation dynamics.

Hardware Engineering and Airborne Antenna Setup

Matthew Thomassen and Sean McKeever share lessons learned configuring high-gain Wi-Fi receivers, GPS logging telemetry, and external antenna mounts inside a Cessna cockpit.

Analyzing High-Altitude Signal Capture and WiGLE Telemetry

Comparing aerial capture datasets with ground-level wardriving data answers key questions regarding access point density, radio signal range at altitude, and flight-level wireless visibility.

Visualizations and Practical Takeaways

Enhanced data visualizations demonstrate the vast geographical footprint of airborne wireless sniffing and highlight privacy implications of urban RF leakage.

talks.title: Running a Software Defined Radio CTF using challengectl
talks.teaser: Explains how the RF Village Capture the Flag team designs wireless challenges and automates over-the-air signal transmission using challengectl.
talks.summary:
The Evolution of RF Capture the Flag Competitions

Software-Defined Radio (SDR) has become a central discipline in cybersecurity competitions, challenging participants to capture, demodulate, and reverse-engineer novel RF signals in real time.

Designing Engaging and Educational RF Challenges

Dan Perret outlines the design philosophy behind RF Village CTF challenges, spanning basic analog modulation, digital telemetry decoding, satellite downlink decoding, and hidden signal steganography.

Automated Signal Transmission with challengectl

RF Hackers Sanctuary engineers developed challengectl, an open-source orchestration tool that schedules, modulates, and transmits multiple concurrent challenge signals across SDR transmitters.

Empowering Communities to Host Wireless Competitions

Releasing open-source CTF transmission software enables schools, hacker conferences, and radio clubs to easily organize their own hands-on wireless security competitions.

talks.title: Open Source Cellular Test Beds for the EFF Rayhunter
talks.teaser: Details building open-source 2G, 4G, and 5G cellular base station testbeds with SDRs to evaluate and benchmark EFF's Rayhunter IMSI catcher detector.
talks.summary:
Benchmarking Cell-Site Simulator Detectors

The Electronic Frontier Foundation’s open-source Rayhunter project turns commercial mobile hotspots into monitors that detect malicious cellular base stations and Stingray interception.

Building Open-Source Cellular Testbeds

Ron Broberg details how researchers deploy open-source software cellular stacks—including OpenAirInterface (OAI) 5G, srsRAN 4G, OpenBTS, and YateBTS—on software-defined radio hardware.

Simulating Rogue Base Station Attacks

Emulating malicious cell-site behaviors (such as forced 2G cipher downgrades, IMSI harvesting, and silent SMS pinging) enables rigorous validation of Rayhunter's detection algorithms.

Advancing Cellular Privacy and Defense

Open testbeds provide an accessible foundation for security researchers to develop and verify new counter-surveillance capabilities against illicit cellular monitoring.

talks.title: McJumpBox: Leveraging Free Corporate Wi-Fi for Fun and Profit
talks.teaser: Reverse engineers commercial 802.11ah Wi-Fi hardware to design a custom solar-powered long-range repeater running OpenWrt for off-grid remote connectivity.
talks.summary:
Exploring Sub-GHz 802.11ah HaLow Wi-Fi

The 802.11ah (Wi-Fi HaLow) standard operates in sub-GHz frequencies (900 MHz), providing long-range, low-power wireless backhaul connections over multiple miles.

Reverse Engineering COTS Modules and Schematics

Loaning evaluates commercial 802.11ah modules, reverse engineering their schematics and firmware constraints to identify hardware design tradeoffs.

Designing Custom Solar-Powered OpenWrt Hardware

Building a custom battery- and solar-powered PCB running OpenWrt bridges 900 MHz sub-GHz backhaul links with standard 2.4 GHz and 5 GHz local Wi-Fi networks.

Operational Deployment and Remote Connectivity

Deploying pairs of repeater nodes enables reliable, long-range remote network bridges by leveraging public Wi-Fi hotspots at commercial establishments.

talks.title: The Dirty Laundry of Stored Value Washing Cards
talks.teaser: Details reverse engineering stored-value contactless laundry cards, uncovering data structure vulnerabilities that allow arbitrary balance modification.
talks.summary:
The Ubiquity of Stored-Value Contactless Cards

Commercial laundry facilities and municipal services worldwide rely on offline stored-value contactless smartcards to process payments without real-time backend network connectivity.

Reverse Engineering RFID Memory Layouts

Aidan Nakache and Equip analyze the internal memory structures, sector keys, and cryptographic checksum algorithms of popular commercial laundry smartcards.

Discovering Balance Modification Flaws

Analyzing memory dumps before and after transactions revealed predictable counter fields and flawed integrity verification, allowing arbitrary balance manipulation.

Global Implications for Offline Payment Systems

The vulnerabilities identified in laundry cards reflect systemic architectural weaknesses across legacy offline stored-value and transit payment systems globally.

talks.title: Airborne WiFi: Rogue Waves in the Sky
talks.teaser: Investigates in-flight commercial airline Wi-Fi infrastructure and Evil Twin rogue access points, detailing SOC analyst detection strategies using ADS-B telemetry.
talks.summary:
The Architecture of In-Flight Airline Wi-Fi

Commercial airliners integrate on-wing satellite radomes, cellular air-to-ground antennas, and cabin wireless access points to provide passenger in-flight internet access.

Evil Twin Rogue Access Points in the Cabin

m0nkeydrag0n recounts real-world discoveries of Evil Twin captive portal attacks deployed aboard commercial passenger flights to harvest passenger credentials mid-flight.

Correlating Cabin Network Telemetry with ADS-B Data

SOC analysts hunting airborne threats must correlate onboard gateway logs, captive portal redirects, and flight telemetry (ADS-B / satellite logs) to pinpoint rogue access points.

Investigative Playbooks for Aviation Cyber Defense

Developing detection heuristics for in-flight networks empowers security analysts to identify deceptive browser portals and protect travelers against airborne cyber attacks.

talks.title: You Might Be a Wardriver If...
talks.teaser: MrBill and CoD_Segfault present a humorous, curated showcase of wardriving antennas, vehicle setups, and community culture from the hacker community.
talks.summary:
DEF CON Security Research Presentation

This talk covers technical security topics and vulnerability research. The presentation includes discussion of contemporary security challenges, demonstrations of exploitation techniques, and insights into defensive countermeasures and security best practices.

(AI summary — Claude Haiku)

talks.title: Small Packet of Bits That Can Save or Destabilize a City
talks.teaser: Analyzes the VHF Weather Radio SAME protocol and seismic alert systems (SASMEX), demonstrating how unauthenticated broadcast signals risk false alarms.
talks.summary:
Origins of VHF Weather Radio and the SAME Protocol

Developed in the 1960s, VHF Weather Radio expanded across North America using the Specific Area Message Encoding (SAME) protocol to broadcast localized emergency alerts.

Integration into Earthquake Warning Systems

In Mexico, SAME broadcasts form the backbone of the Mexican Seismic Alert System (SASMEX), warning over 30 million citizens seconds before earthquake tremors arrive.

Building Custom SDR Receivers and Protocol Decoding

Manuel Rabid details the engineering of custom VHF receivers, analyzing FSK audio subcarrier modulation and header packet structures used to transmit emergency codes.

Lack of Cryptographic Origin Authentication

Because legacy SAME broadcasts lack digital signatures or cryptographic origin verification, low-cost SDR transmitters can easily spoof emergency alerts, highlighting urgent infrastructure security needs.

talks.title: Meshtastic Command & Control
talks.teaser: Eric Escobar details building an out-of-band command-and-control infrastructure using $25 Meshtastic LoRa radios to manage remote Linux dropboxes.
talks.summary:
Out-of-Band Remote Host Management

Maintaining reliable command-and-control (C2) to remote physical dropboxes or isolated hardware in denied network environments presents major connectivity challenges.

Meshtastic LoRa as an Out-of-Band C2 Channel

Eric Escobar demonstrates how low-cost ($25) LoRa hardware and the open Meshtastic mesh network can serve as a decentralized, long-range command transport.

Executing Remote Shell Commands Over LoRa

Encoding encrypted terminal commands and diagnostic scripts into LoRa text messages enables operators to manage Linux endpoints without cellular modems or local Wi-Fi.

Operational Advantages and Constraints

While constrained by low LoRa bandwidth, Meshtastic C2 provides a resilient, off-grid communication channel for troubleshooting, exfiltration, and stealthy endpoint management.

talks.title: Layer 2 Liberation: Things Your AP Never Dreamed Of
talks.teaser: Allan Riordan Ball demonstrates bypassing SSIDs, handshakes, and IP stacks to sling raw 802.11 frames with Scapy as a peer-to-peer data transport pipe.
talks.summary:
Bypassing Higher Network Layers

Allan Riordan Ball explores subverting the traditional Wi-Fi model by stripping away SSIDs, authentication handshakes, and IP routing to treat 802.11 strictly as a blank RF data pipe.

Crafting Raw 802.11 Frames with Scapy

Using Python and Scapy alongside standard USB Wi-Fi adapters in monitor and injection modes, Ball constructs custom management and action frames capable of arbitrary data payload delivery.

Practical Point-to-Point Wireless Hacks

The presentation demonstrates practical wireless hacks including ad-hoc file transfers, covert signaling, and beacon stuffing without requiring an intervening access point.

Detection and Defensive Implications

Because raw frame transmissions bypass typical firewalling and connection logging, detecting non-standard layer 2 traffic requires specialized RF monitoring and frame-level anomaly detection.
